deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the core of a proof of the Hölder inequality for Schatten–von Neumann classes, the 'formule (6)' of the previous page. The claim is ||AB||_r <= ||A||_p ||B||_q when 1/p+1/q = 1/r, with A in L^p and B in L^q. Here S_p(A) = Tr|A|^p = sum of s_i(A)^p.

Notation from the previous pages:
- L = (AB)^*(AB), H = A^*A, K = B^*B.
- For a positive trace-class operator T, M_T(rho) = sum_n alpha_n(T) rho^n. Here alpha_n(T) is the n-th elementary symmetric function of the eigenvalues of T. So M_T(rho) = det(1+rho T), the Fredholm determinant.
- Formula (9) is the Mellin-transform identity: for 0<s<1, the integral from 0 to infinity of log det(1+rho T) rho^{-1-s} d rho equals (lambda(s)/s) S_s(T). This comes from the scalar integral of log(1+rho x) rho^{-1-s} over (0, infinity), which equals x^s pi/(s sin(pi s)).
- Consistency with the formulas on this page forces lambda(x) = pi/sin(pi x).
- m is an integer chosen with p, q <= 2m, so that s = r/2m, p/2m, q/2m all lie in (0,1). Then S_r(AB) = S_{r/2m}(L^m), S_p(A) = S_{p/2m}(H^m), S_q(B) = S_{q/2m}(K^m).
- Lemma 2 gives alpha_n(L^m) <= alpha_n(H^m) alpha_n(K^m). This is a Weyl–Horn / exterior-power type inequality for singular values.

Steps on this page.
1. Since r/p + r/q = 1, rho^n = rho^{nr/p} rho^{nr/q}. All terms are nonnegative, so M_{L^m}(rho) <= M_{H^m}(rho^{r/p}) M_{K^m}(rho^{r/q}).
2. Take logs and integrate against rho^{-1-r/2m}. Using (11)/(12) this gives (13): (lambda(r/2m)/(r/2m)) S_r(AB) <= the integral of log M_{H^m}(rho^{r/p}) rho^{-1-r/2m} d rho plus the analogous K-integral.
3. Substitute sigma = rho^{r/p}. Then d rho/rho = (p/r) d sigma/sigma and rho^{r/2m} = sigma^{p/2m}. The first integral becomes (p/r)(lambda(p/2m)/(p/2m)) S_{p/2m}(H^m) = (lambda(p/2m)/(r/2m)) S_p(A). The second integral is handled the same way.
4. Hence lambda(r/2m) S_r(AB) <= lambda(p/2m) S_p(A) + lambda(q/2m) S_q(B). Equivalently, S_r(AB) <= [sin(pi r/2m)/sin(pi p/2m)] S_p(A) + [sin(pi r/2m)/sin(pi q/2m)] S_q(B). A marginal remark notes this also yields finiteness of S_r(AB).
5. Let m -> infinity. The sine ratios tend to r/p and r/q, giving (14): Tr|AB|^r <= (r/p) Tr|A|^p + (r/q) Tr|B|^q. This is a trace-level Young inequality.
6. Grothendieck remarks it is 'remarkable but not the one we seek'. On the next page he rescales A -> lambda A, B -> mu B and optimizes over lambda, mu. This recovers S_r(AB) <= S_p(A)^{r/p} S_q(B)^{r/q}, i.e. Hölder.
errors: Not an error of Grothendieck: in the second line the factor should be M_{K^m}(rho^{q^{-1}r}); the transcription's M_H is a misreading.

The definition of lambda as transcribed on the previous page, pi/(x sin(pi x)), is inconsistent with this page. Formulas (13) and the sine-ratio form require lambda(x) = pi/sin(pi x). Either the earlier transcription or an earlier draft definition is off.
Minor gap: justifying the passage to M_{L^m} <= product of the two series for infinite-dimensional operators, and finiteness of the integrals, is only sketched in a marginal remark.
Minor gap: the needed range 0 < r/2m, p/2m, q/2m < 1 (convergence of the Mellin integral) is implicit in the choice of m.

ideas.what: Representing Schatten quasi-norms S_s(T) for 0<s<1 as a Mellin transform of log det(1+rho T)
ideas.modern_name: Mellin/Stieltjes integral representation of power traces via Fredholm determinants
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (the integral of log(1+x) x^{-1-s} is Euler-type); its use for Schatten classes appears in Gohberg–Krein-style determinant theory
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) or Produits tensoriels topologiques, ch. II; unsure if this exact argument appears

ideas.what: Raising to the power m and letting m -> infinity to linearize inequalities between elementary symmetric functions of singular values
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Weyl 1949, A. Horn 1950, Ky Fan 1951
Follows from Schatten–Hölder plus scalar AM–GM; the stronger singular-value form is due to T. Ando (1995)

ideas.what: Hölder inequality for Schatten classes, obtained from the Young form by homogeneity
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for Schatten–von Neumann ideals
ideas.where_published: Possibly Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), discussion of p-summable operators

missed.claim: This is an unusual, self-contained proof of the Schatten–Hölder inequality. It uses Fredholm determinants det(1+rho T), a Mellin-transform representation of Tr T^s for s in (0,1), and an m -> infinity limit of sine ratios. The route is not the standard one (interpolation or majorization) and seems not to be recorded as Grothendieck's.
missed.quote: Faisant tendre m vers +infini, on obtient la formule plus simple (14) S_r(AB) <= r/p S_p(A) + r/q S_q(B)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck linking Fredholm determinant theory to Schatten-ideal inequalities in 1953. Mathematically the result is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The result (Schatten–Hölder, and its trace-Young form) is classical by 1953. Only the determinant/Mellin-transform proof technique is a mildly interesting unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: '= M_{H^m}(rho^{p^{-1}r}) M_H(rho^{q^{-1}r})' should read M_{H^m}(rho^{p^{-1}r}) M_{K^m}(rho^{q^{-1}r}).

The parenthetical after the sine formula appears to read roughly 'cela vérifie a fortiori S_r(AB) < +infini, et donc justifie ... (finitude) si S_p(A), S_q(B) finis'. The machine reading 'S_p(AB) <= +infini' is doubtful.
In the line 'p r^{-1} lambda(p/2m)/(p/2m) S_{p/2m}(H^m) = lambda(p/2m)/(r/2m) S_p(A)', the crossed-out 'lambda(p)' is correctly marked as deleted.
Last line: 'C'est une inégalité remarquable, mais ce n'est pas celle que nous cherchons. Mais ...' (a 'ce' is likely missing in the transcription).
